clue.text: Flyer's pace with winds

indicators.note: winds as in twists and turns, so the letters of the words before it are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes how fast a pilot or bird travels with the wind behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer's' reads as possessive; it is 'Flyer is'. 'winds' looks like the weather but is the anagram signal on PACE WITH.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitecap is a bird name, used for the white-crowned sparrow and for the redstart.

clue.text: Little time to put on top half of underwear (shift)

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a little time

indicators.note: the first two of the four letters of the garment word, its upper half in a down entry

parts.note: a vest is an undergarment in British English, a singlet

explanation.surface: A rushed instruction to pull on a vest, with 'shift' as a stray old word for a chemise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a garment (an old word for a slip), fitting the underwear picture, but it is the definition as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To move something is to shift it, change its place or position.

clue.text: Old actor's theatrical entry point?

definitions.meaning: an old hand at the stage, a seasoned performer; the usual phrase
whimsically, a thing that gets something onto the stage, i.e. one that stages a play

explanation.surface: A question about where a veteran performer comes on.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is playful: a stager as one who puts on (stages) a show, the question mark warning the sense is stretched.
explanation.definitionFit: A stager is an experienced person, especially a veteran performer of the theatre.

clue.text: Make negative positive? That's progress

definitions.meaning: in photography a film negative is processed to bring out the image, giving prints
to move forward or grow, as a skill or a plan does

explanation.surface: A cheery motto: turning bad into good counts as progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negative' reads as pessimism but is a photographic negative.
explanation.definitionFit: Developing film turns latent negatives into pictures; to develop also means to advance or mature.

clue.text: Excited about getting over

parts.note: up as in worked up, excited
on as in a talk on a subject, about it

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled about recovering from something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting over' looks like the definition (recovering), but 'getting' is a link and 'over' alone is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Upon is a preposition meaning on top of, so it can stand for over.

clue.text: Direction on getting seduced is not finished

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on the second

parts.note: left is a direction, like right
undone in the old sense of ruined by seduction

explanation.surface: A melodramatic tale of someone led astray, left incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: Work that is left undone is incomplete, unfinished business.

clue.text: Coral's a devotee of the drink

indicators.note: a devotee of the sea puts the sea word first, as in a sports fan named by his sport

parts.note: the drink is slang for the sea
a fan is a devotee or enthusiast

explanation.surface: Someone called Coral is said to love a tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coral' poses as a woman's name. 'the drink' is informal for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea fans are fan-shaped gorgonian corals that grow on reefs.

clue.text: Gag: "Time to be replaced by sun bird"

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out for another named after this phrase

parts.note: to gag can mean to choke or strangle, i.e. to throttle
S is the abbreviation for sun, as on weather maps or for Sunday

explanation.surface: A joke or instruction about time giving way to sunshine for a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the Ts (the second) becomes S.
explanation.definitionFit: Throstle is an old and poetic name for the song thrush.

clue.text: Cook's offering coated egg starters, man!

parts.note: a pie is something a cook serves up

indicators.note: starters are first courses, so here the opening letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A cook serves a pie with breadcrumbed eggs, and an exclamation follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man!' looks like an exclamation; it means a chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess piece is commonly called a man, as are draughts counters.

clue.text: Under-the-table activity is said to be a financial indicator

indicators.note: said marks a word heard rather than written

parts.note: playing footsie is flirtatious foot-touching under a table

explanation.surface: Playing footsie as a hot market tip.
explanation.walkthrough: The FTSE 100 is London's main share index, pronounced 'footsie'.
explanation.definitionFit: The FTSE 100 index tracks the largest shares on the London Stock Exchange, a market gauge.

clue.text: Party takes volcanic rock to be healthy food

indicators.note: the party word is followed by the rock word it takes on

parts.note: the Greens are a political party
tuff is rock formed from volcanic ash

explanation.surface: A political party adopts a lump of lava as its health food.
explanation.definitionFit: Green stuff is informal for vegetables, especially leafy greens, healthy eating.

clue.text: Round fired by low-powered transporter — duck!

indicators.note: fired in the sense of dismissed, so the round letter is ejected from the vehicle word

parts.note: a scooter is a small, low-powered motorcycle
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A shot comes from a passing moped, so take cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck!' reads as a warning to dodge the round; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoter is a dark sea duck of northern coasts.

clue.text: Want erotic stimulation? It could enhance the spirit

indicators.note: stimulation stirs things up, so these letters are agitated into new order

explanation.surface: A saucy question followed by an uplifting promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' reads as mood or soul, but means gin or vodka.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic is the classic mixer for gin and other spirits, improving the drink.

clue.text: Pop off before a bid for the other side

indicators.note: the jumbled piece comes ahead of the bid
off as in gone bad or not right, so the three letters are jumbled

parts.note: one no-trump, written 1NT, is a bridge bid

explanation.surface: Someone nips out before making an offer for the rival team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop off' looks like 'leave'; 'off' is the anagram signal on POP, giving OPP. 'a bid' is the bridge call one no-trumps, written ONE NT.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is on the opposing team or side in a contest.

clue.text: Secure parking at home

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
in means at home, not out

explanation.surface: Make sure your car is parked safely at the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To pin is to fasten or hold something securely in place.

clue.text: Supposing one's knocked out by Earth's opportunity?

indicators.note: the letter for one is knocked out and the letter after this phrase takes its place

parts.note: opining is offering an opinion, supposing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A boxer imagines a knockout delivered by the planet itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The first I of OPINING becomes E.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is a chance or opportunity, as a job opening.

clue.text: That is taken from vacuous pet name

indicators.note: the abbreviation's letters are removed from the following word

parts.note: inane means empty-headed, vacuous
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a silly name being dropped from a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet name' looks like a vacuous name for an animal; it is a familiar name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nan is an affectionate familiar name for a grandmother, or a diminutive of Ann.

clue.text: What invaders hope to make

parts.note: invading armies push forward into enemy land along roads, so they make literal advances into territory

explanation.surface: An invading army's ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'make inroads' means gain ground, and for invaders it is literal too.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are hostile advances or raids into territory, and figuratively progress.

clue.text: Slanting support raised along breaks

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: aid is help or support

indicators.note: breaks as in shatters, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sloping brace is lifted while something snaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AID into DIA; 'breaks' rearranges ALONG as GONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagonal line slants across from corner to corner, at an angle.

clue.text: Journalist bowled over by criminal plea

indicators.note: by as in beside, the one piece next to the other
knocked over, so the letters are turned round, read upwards in a down entry

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
a fence is a criminal who receives stolen goods

explanation.surface: A reporter knocked down by a crook makes a plea in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plea' is the legal sense: a defendant's case.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a plea is the defence a defendant puts forward in answer to a charge.

clue.text: Beginning one's comeback, one abandons discipline

indicators.note: a comeback returns, so the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: an, the indefinite article, means one

indicators.note: the letter for one walks out of the next word

parts.note: a science is a discipline or field of study
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sportsman starting a comeback quits a training regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's comeback' gives NA (one = AN, reversed) and ''s' is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascence is the state of coming into being, an origin or start.

clue.text: Belligerent act from America's leader: time to change course

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: to tack is to change course by turning a sailing boat into the wind

explanation.surface: A US president's military reversal, framed as a political jab.
explanation.definitionFit: An attack is an aggressive assault, a hostile military action.

clue.text: Ms West, wild and frenzied woman

parts.note: Mae West was the American film star of the 1930s

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so the next word's letters run out of order

explanation.surface: Mae West portrayed as a wild, frenzied woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A maenad was a frenzied female follower of Bacchus, hence any raving woman.

clue.text: Married giant — disastrous wedding

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married, as in genealogies

indicators.note: a disastrous outcome means things in a mess, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A tabloid line: a giant gets hitched and the wedding is a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Mating is pairing up or coupling, as wedding joins two in union.

clue.text: Meant to chat about releasing ring accessory

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters are turned around and reordered
releasing lets go of one letter from the pool before the rest are rearranged

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone planned to talk about removing a ring from their outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove an O from MEANT TO CHAT and rearrange what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: An attachment is an extra part fitted to a tool or device, an add-on.

clue.text: Increase steps taken

definitions.meaning: a rise, as in prices or rates
a long walk across country, many paces taken

explanation.surface: A notice that steps are being taken to increase something.
explanation.definitionFit: A price hike is a rise; a hike is also a long country walk.

clue.text: Jumper cut at back end — rip off!

parts.note: a roo is a kangaroo, the jumping animal, with its name cut short

indicators.note: the end is the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A sweater shortened at the back is a complete swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' (British for a sweater) is the kangaroo, whose name cut short is ROO; 'end' takes the last letter of 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to cheat or swindle them, an old slang verb.

clue.text: Author's not in, causing row

indicators.note: not means without, so the two-letter word is cut from the author's name

parts.note: Ian Rankin is the Scottish crime author of the Rebus novels

explanation.surface: A writer is out, which leads to a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel; it means a line or tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank is a line of people or things, a row, as a taxi rank.

clue.text: Control tongue, when speaking

indicators.note: speaking means the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: Czech is a language, a tongue

explanation.surface: Advice to hold your tongue while talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' reads as the body part but means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to restrain or curb it, keeping it under control.

clue.text: Prison supported by city with body of rules

parts.note: can is slang for prison
on as in resting on, supported by
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A jail backed by a city authority and its regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: Canon law is the code of laws governing a church.
